newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH EXPORTERS WANT 20-25 PCT DEVALUATION -SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH EXPORTERS WANT 20-25 PCT DEVALUATION -SURVEY.

text.p: Czech exporters said, among other suggestions, that they would want a 20 to 25 percent devalution of the crown against a mark/dollar basket to help boost lagging exports in 1997, according to survey by the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) obtained on Tuesday.
The survey was conducted in November among 170 Czech companies who provide 34 percent of the country's exports.

In comments to the CSU survey, the exporters said that if there would not be a devaluation of the still strong Czech currency, then they expect the governmnet to adopt bureaucratic measures to regulate imports.
The trade deficit is expected to top 162 billion crowns in 1996, the survey said, and analysts have forecast the 1997 trade gap topping 200 billion crowns.

Official data from CSU showed the deficit for the eleven-month period ending November 1996 at 140 billion crowns, up from 81 billion for the same pariod in 1995, with the exports totalling 549 billion and imports 670 billion crowns.
CSU said the exporters expected that crown would not be stable in 1997,
In devaluation they see better conditions for exports which would raise the total volume of exports and the profit.
In the meantime imports would become more expensive and also limited, which could have positive influence on lowering the trade deficit.
Devaluation would however also make imported strategical raw materials more expensive and transport costs and other foreign services would become more expensive which could lower incomes.
